title: Linux_Remaiten_Botnet_Investigation_f1b
description: Investigate a potential botnet infection, identify compromised systems, determine command-and-control infrastructure, and implement containment measures.
prerequisites: Basic knowledge of Linux system administration
Basic knowledge of network security analysis
outcomes: Usage of systemctl for service management
Usage of ss for network connection analysis
Usage of tcpdump for network traffic analysis

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: The network has experienced unusual traffic patterns and performance degradation. Initial investigations suggest a potential botnet infection. Your task is to identify and analyze the compromised systems, determine the command-and-control infrastructure, and implement containment measures. The specific malware family under investigation is Linux/Remaiten, known for its periodic external communication and flooding capabilities. Linux/Remaiten typically uses a persistent service to maintain its presence and communicates with a command-and-control server to receive instructions and exfiltrate data.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content:
You have SSH access to the bot1 host with the following credentials:
- Username: cyrano
- Password: cyrano
levels.local_content: Local sandbox access is not required for this scenario.

levels.title: Identify Suspicious Service
levels.content:
Identify and investigate an unauthorized or suspicious service responsible for periodic external communication.

**Question:** What is the name of the suspicious service that communicates with an external host? (Flag type: service name)
levels.solution: Check running services and look for unusual network connections. The suspicious service is named `bot-beacon.service`. The flag type is a service name.

hints.title: Conceptual Hint
hints.content: Consider checking the running services on the system to identify any unusual or unauthorized services.

hints.title: Directional Hint
hints.content: Use the command `systemctl list-units --type=service` to list all running services.

hints.title: Near-Spoiler Hint
hints.content: Look for services that are not part of the standard system services. The suspicious service is named `bot-beacon.service`.

levels.title: Determine Command-and-Control Server
levels.content:
Determine the external host communicating with the compromised system.

**Question:** What is the IP address of the command-and-control server? (Flag type: IP address)
levels.solution: Investigate network connections and look for unusual destinations. The command-and-control server is at IP address `192.168.70.5`. The flag type is an IP address.

hints.title: Conceptual Hint
hints.content: Investigate the network connections to identify any unusual or unauthorized external communications.

hints.title: Directional Hint
hints.content: Use the command `ss -tulnp` to investigate network connections.

hints.title: Near-Spoiler Hint
hints.content: Look for connections to the IP address `192.168.70.5`.

levels.title: Identify Target of Flood Attack
levels.content:
Identify the system receiving the abnormal volume of network traffic generated by the compromised host.

**Question:** What is the IP address of the system being targeted by the flood attack? (Flag type: IP address)
levels.solution: Analyze network flows to determine the victim of the flooding activity. The target system is at IP address `192.168.80.100`. The flag type is an IP address.

hints.title: Conceptual Hint
hints.content: Analyze the network flows to identify any systems receiving an abnormal volume of traffic.

hints.title: Directional Hint
hints.content: Use the command `tcpdump -i any` to analyze network flows.

hints.title: Near-Spoiler Hint
hints.content: Look for traffic directed to the IP address `192.168.80.100`.
